title: Countably generated projectivity descends faithfully flatly
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], and let $P$ be an $A$-module. If the $B$-module $B\otimes_A P$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] is countably generated and projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], then $P$ is countably generated and projective over $A$. Here countably generated means generated by an at most countable subset under finite linear combinations; neither $P$ nor its scalar extension is assumed finitely generated or finitely presented. The $B$-action on the tensor product is $b\cdot(b'\otimes p)=bb'\otimes p$.

proof.text: Put $N=B\otimes_A P$. Choose a generating family $(y_i)_{i\in I}$ of $N$ with $I$ at most countable. By the finite pure-tensor presentation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], write $y_i=\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}b_{ij}\otimes p_{ij}$. The pairs $(i,j)$ form an at most countable set (finite sets over a countable index set). Let $P_0\subseteq P$ be the submodule spanned by the $p_{ij}$. The image of $B\otimes_A P_0\to N$ is a $B$-submodule: multiplying $b\otimes p$ by $c$ gives $cb\otimes p$ in the same image. This image contains every $y_i$, hence is $N$. Thus tensoring the complex $P_0\to P\to0$ with $B$ makes it exact at $N$. Faithful exactness in [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] makes the original complex exact at $P$, so $P_0=P$. This proves countable generation of $P$, including the empty generating-set case.

proof.text: Projectivity of $N$ implies flatness over $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flatness-descends-faithfully-flat] with $R=A$, $R\prime=B$, and $M=P$. Its scalar extension is exactly $N$ with the stipulated first-factor action, so $P$ is flat over $A$.

proof.text: We verify directly that the projective $B$-module $N$ is Mittag-Leffler. By [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], choose a free $F=\bigoplus_{t\in T}B$ and maps $i:N\to F$, $s:F\to N$ with $si=1$. For any $B$-module $Q$, the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identifies $F\otimes_B Q$ with finitely supported families in $Q$: $e_t\otimes q$ is the family with $q$ at $t$ and zero elsewhere, with inverse $(q_t)\mapsto\sum_t e_t\otimes q_t$. Consequently for any family $(Q_j)_j$ the map $\theta_F$ of [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module] sends a finitely supported family of tuples $(q_{t,j})_j$ to its coordinate families $(q_{t,j})_t$. If its image is zero, every $q_{t,j}=0$, hence the original family is zero. Thus $\theta_F$ is injective. If $x\in N\otimes_B\prod_j Q_j$ has $\theta_N(x)=0$, naturality on pure tensors gives $\theta_F((i\otimes1)x)=\prod_j(i\otimes1)(\theta_N(x))=0$. Injectivity just proved gives $(i\otimes1)x=0$, and applying $s\otimes1$ gives $x=0$. Therefore $N$ is Mittag-Leffler.

proof.text: Step 1 gives countable generation of $P$, Step 2 gives flatness, and Step 4 gives the Mittag-Leffler property. These are all the hypotheses of [lem-trf-countable-flat-mittag-leffler-projective] with $R=A$. Hence $P$ is projective over $A$. Together with Step 1 this proves both conclusions, without a finite-generation or finite-presentation assumption.
